blocks.text: Government schemes are launched to tackle social and economic problems, and banks are the delivery channel for most of them. That is why every banking exam asks about them: who launched what, when, for whom and with what limit. Start with the calendar below, then use the comparison table as your master sheet. (Statistics in this chapter are the figures quoted in the 2024-25 study material and will have moved on since.)

blocks.title: Launch calendar
items: NREGA enacted; phased in from 200 districts (2006) to the whole country by 2008
PM announces Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) as a National Mission on Financial Inclusion
PMJJBY, PMSBY and Atal Pension Yojana launched together
Gold Monetization Scheme, Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme and Indian Gold Coin launched
Ujala Yojana launched in Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh)
Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY) opens for subscription (till 3 May 2018, later extended)
Rs 500 per month for three months announced for women Jan Dhan account holders (Covid-19 relief)
Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan announced in four tranches
PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan launched

blocks.title: Master comparison: scheme, launch, eligibility, benefit
rows: Every unbanked household; no minimum balance
Basic account, RuPay card with Rs 2 lakh accident cover, overdraft after 6 months
Age 18-50 with bank account and auto-debit consent
Rs 2 lakh life cover (death for any reason); premium Rs 330 a year (as per the source)
Age 18-70 with bank account and auto-debit consent
Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability, Rs 1 lakh partial; premium Rs 12 a year
Age 18-40 with savings or post office savings account
Guaranteed monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 from age 60
Small and micro businesses, first-generation entrepreneurs
Collateral-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun)
Bank loans of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore
Assured 8% return for 10 years, pension up to Rs 10,000 a month

blocks.title: The 9th May trio
blocks.phrase: Jan Dhan opens the door; on 9 May three guards walk in: Jeevan, Suraksha, Atal - Life, Accident, Age.
letters: Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana - life cover
Atal Pension Yojana - pension for old age
blocks.note: Mudra is NOT in the trio: it came a month earlier, on 8 April 2015.

blocks.text: PMJDY was announced by the Prime Minister in his Independence Day speech on **15 August 2014** as the **National Mission on Financial Inclusion**. The aim is comprehensive inclusion of every household: universal access to banking with at least one basic bank account per household, plus financial literacy, access to credit, insurance and pension. The tagline is **Mera Khata Bhagya Vidhata** and the focus unit is the household. Around 1.5 crore accounts were opened on the day of launch.

blocks.title: What a Jan Dhan account unlocks
items: No minimum balance; small account if no KYC papers
Inbuilt accident cover of Rs 2 lakh
PMJJBY, PMSBY and APY via the account

blocks.title: Key features
items: A person with no savings account can open one without any minimum balance.
Anyone who self-certifies that they lack officially valid documents may open a **small account**.
Over 6 lakh villages were mapped into **1.59 lakh Sub Service Areas (SSAs)**; each SSA typically has 1,000 to 1,500 households.
In the **1.26 lakh SSAs without a bank branch**, Bank Mitras (business correspondents) were deployed for branchless banking.
Overdraft facility is available after six months of satisfactory account operation or credit history; the limit was doubled from Rs 5,000 to **Rs 10,000**.
Financial literacy programmes give the unbanked awareness of financial products.

blocks.title: Covid-19 relief
blocks.text: On 26 March 2020, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced **Rs 500 per month for three months** to every woman Jan Dhan account holder to offset the loss caused by the Covid-19 outbreak.

blocks.title: What a Jan Dhan account gives you
blocks.phrase: Jan Dhan gives you a BROI: Basic account, RuPay card, Overdraft, Insurance - 'Bro, I am banked!'
letters: Basic account with no minimum balance
Overdraft of Rs 10,000 after six months
Insurance: Rs 2 lakh accident cover on the card

sections.title: From Jan Dhan to Jan Suraksha: PMJJBY and PMSBY

blocks.text: To build a universal social security system for the poor and under-privileged, the Prime Minister launched three schemes in insurance and pension on **9 May 2015**: PMJJBY (life insurance), PMSBY (accident insurance) and APY (pension). The two insurance schemes are covered here; the pension scheme has its own section.

blocks.title: PMJJBY vs PMSBY
rows: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
Rs 2 lakh on death of the insured for any reason
Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability; Rs 1 lakh for partial disability
Rs 330 a year (as per the source)
LIC and other life insurers willing to offer it
Public sector general insurers and other willing general insurers

blocks.title: Common rules
items: Both need a bank account; Aadhaar is the primary KYC for that account.
The subscriber consents to join and enables **auto-debit** on or before 31 May for the coverage year.
Coverage year is **1 June to 31 May** and renews annually.
The premium is auto-debited from the account in one instalment.
Insurers must tie up with banks to offer the product on similar terms.

blocks.text: Do not mix the two: **Jeevan = Life** (age limit 50, LIC, Rs 330) and **Suraksha = Safety from accidents** (age limit 70, general insurers, Rs 12). Premiums were revised upward in 2022, so read exam stems for the figure they quote.

blocks.title: Age limits and premiums
blocks.phrase: Life to Fifty, Safety to Seventy, Atal to Forty - all start at eighteen. Jeevan costs 330, Suraksha just a dozen.
letters: 18-50 years; Rs 330; Rs 2 lakh life cover
18-70 years; Rs 12; Rs 2 lakh / Rs 1 lakh accident cover

blocks.text: APY was launched by the Prime Minister on **9 May 2015**. It is open to all savings bank or post office savings bank account holders aged **18 to 40 years**; the contribution depends on the pension amount chosen and the age of joining.

blocks.title: Key facts
rows: Savings bank or post office savings bank account holder, age 18-40
Subscriber first, then spouse; after both, the corpus accumulated by age 60 goes to the nominee
The Central Government funds any shortfall if returns are lower than estimated
If returns are higher, the subscriber gets enhanced pension benefits
Spouse may continue contributing until the subscriber would have turned 60 and gets the same pension
Public sector banks, private banks, Regional Rural Banks, cooperative banks and the Department of Posts
149.53 lakh subscribers with total pension wealth of Rs 6,860.30 crore

blocks.title: Who is paid, in order
items: The subscriber receives the guaranteed monthly pension from age 60.
After the subscriber's death, the spouse receives the same pension.
After the death of both, the corpus accumulated till age 60 is returned to the nominee.

blocks.title: Order of payment under APY
blocks.phrase: S-S-N: Subscriber, then Spouse, then Nominee gets the lump sum. Pension is 1 to 5 thousand - count 1-2-3-4-5.
letters: Spouse - same pension after the subscriber

sections.title: Mudra Yojana and Stand Up India

blocks.text: Both schemes push institutional credit to people who normally struggle to borrow. **PMMY (Mudra)** was launched on **8 April 2015** and gives collateral-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh in three bands. **Stand Up India** was launched on **5 April 2016** and backs first-time entrepreneurs from SC/ST and women.

blocks.title: Mudra facts
items: Aim: build the confidence of young, educated or skilled workers to become first-generation entrepreneurs, and help existing small businesses expand.
Sanctioned by 31.03.2019: Rs 3,21,722 crore in 5.99 crore accounts (Shishu Rs 142,345 crore; Kishore Rs 104,386 crore; Tarun Rs 74,991 crore).

blocks.title: Stand Up India facts
rows: At least one SC/ST borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch
Setting up greenfield (new) enterprises in manufacturing, services or trading
All Scheduled Commercial Banks; target of at least 2.5 lakh borrowers
Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand Up India (CGFSI)
Handholding support, convergence with Central/State schemes, ready and trainee borrowers covered
Applications can be made on the Stand Up Mitra portal (standupmitra.in)
Rs 16,085 crore sanctioned in 72,983 accounts (59,429 women, 3,103 ST, 10,451 SC)

blocks.title: Mudra's three sizes
blocks.phrase: Baby, Teen, Adult: Shishu is the baby (up to 50k), Kishore the teen (50k-5 lakh), Tarun the young adult (5-10 lakh).
letters: Tarun - Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh
blocks.note: Stand Up India is a '1+1' scheme: one SC/ST and one woman borrower per branch, Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore.

blocks.text: The **Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY)** protects people aged **60 years and above** from a fall in interest income when market conditions are uncertain, and gives social security in old age. It is implemented through the **Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)**.

blocks.title: PMVVY details
rows: Assured return of 8% per annum for 10 years
Monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annual, as chosen by the subscriber
Minimum purchase price Rs 1.5 lakh per family for Rs 1,000 a month; maximum Rs 7.5 lakh per family for Rs 5,000 a month
Extended up to 31 March 2020; cap raised to Rs 15 lakh per senior citizen

blocks.title: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS)
blocks.text: The maximum deposit limit under SCSS was raised from **Rs 15 lakh to Rs 30 lakh**, effective **1 April 2023**, in line with Budget 2023. SCSS is one of the government small savings schemes, which exist to give the public safe, attractive investment options while mobilising resources for development.

blocks.title: PMVVY in three numbers
blocks.phrase: Sixty, Eight, Ten: sixty-year-olds get eight per cent for ten years - and LIC pays the bill.
letters: Assured return, per cent a year
Policy term in years (max pension Rs 10,000 a month)

blocks.text: Three gold schemes were announced in Budget 2015-16 and launched by the Prime Minister on **5 November 2015**. Together they aim to mobilise India's idle gold, give households a paper alternative to physical gold, and promote Indian-minted coins.

blocks.title: The three gold schemes
rows: Mobilise gold lying idle with households and trusts and use it productively
Gold jewellery makers (mostly small and medium units) get gold; common people earn interest on their gold
New investment instrument; reduce the demand for physical gold
In the long run cuts gold imports; first tranche open 6-30 Nov 2015 raised about Rs 250 crore
Promote indigenously minted national gold coins
Aligned with the Make in India programme

blocks.title: Tax-free bonds (FY 2015-16)
items: Government allowed tax-free bonds worth **Rs 40,000 crore** in 2015-16.
Issuers include NHAI, IRFC, HUDCO, IREDA, PFC, REC and NTPC.

Eligible investors: retail individual investors (RIIs), qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), corporates including statutory corporations, trusts, partnership firms, LLPs, cooperative banks, Regional Rural Banks and other legal entities, and high net-worth individuals (HNIs).

blocks.title: Tax-free bond issuers
blocks.phrase: New India Houses In Pretty Rural Neighbourhoods.
letters: NHAI - National Highways Authority of India
HUDCO - Housing and Urban Development Corporation
IREDA - Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency
blocks.note: The three gold schemes share one date: 5 November 2015.

sections.title: Startup India, Sustainable Finance and JIVA

blocks.title: Startup India
rows: Flagship initiative to catalyse startup culture and build an inclusive ecosystem for innovation and entrepreneurship
Turn India into a country of job creators instead of job seekers
A dedicated Startup India Team reporting to the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT); the source writes it as Industrial Policy and Promotion
Build a strong ecosystem for startup growth, sustainable economic growth and large-scale employment
Incubation centres, easier patent filing, tax exemptions, ease of setting up a business, a Rs 10,000 crore corpus fund and a faster exit mechanism

blocks.title: SIDBI Sustainable Finance Scheme
rows: Fund sustainable development projects (energy efficiency, cleaner production) not covered by international or bilateral credit lines
Renewable energy, BEE star rating, green microfinance, green buildings, eco-friendly labelling
New or existing MSMEs as defined under the MSMED Act 2006
Satisfactory track record and sound finances, no default to banks, minimum credit rating of investment grade
Renewable plants (solar, wind, mini hydel, biomass gasifier), waste-management cleaner-production investments, and OEMs of green machinery that are MSMEs or supply many MSMEs

blocks.title: JIVA programme
blocks.text: **NABARD** launched JIVA on **9 February 2022** to promote **natural farming** under its watershed and wadi programmes. It is an agro-ecology-based programme in **11 states** across five agro-ecological zones that are ecologically fragile and rain-fed.

blocks.title: Who runs which green scheme
blocks.phrase: SIDBI keeps Small industry Sustainable; NABARD farms Naturally with JIVA - 'Bank for Agriculture' = natural farming.
letters: Home of the Startup India team

sections.title: Gati Shakti, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Ujala

blocks.title: PM Gati Shakti - National Master Plan
rows: 13 October 2021 by PM Narendra Modi at Pragati Maidan, New Delhi
Multi-modal connectivity and integrated planning of infrastructure
Brings 16 ministries, including rail and roadways, together
Infrastructure schemes of ministries and states such as Bharatmala, Sagarmala and UDAN
Textile clusters, pharmaceutical clusters, defence corridors, fishing clusters, Agrizones

blocks.title: Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan (Self-Reliant India)
rows: May 2020, in four tranches, by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman
Economic stimulus and relief package of about Rs 20 lakh crore
MSMEs, cottage industries, middle class, migrants, industry and more

blocks.title: Ujala Yojana
rows: 30 April 2016 in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh (as per the source)
Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL), a joint venture of PSUs under the Union Ministry of Power
Promote energy efficiency; cut consumers' electricity bills, support energy security and protect the environment

blocks.title: Sixteen ministries on one platform
blocks.phrase: Gati Shakti = speed plus power: 13-10-2021, sixteen ministries, one digital map.

blocks.text: **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** was launched on **1 January 2013**. Subsidies under various social schemes are sent directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries, with the Aadhaar number linked to the beneficiary database so that ghost and duplicate names are weeded out.

blocks.title: How a DBT payment travels
items: Duplicates removed; only genuine names remain
APB moves funds on the Aadhaar number
Subsidy credited straight to the person

blocks.title: MGNREGS facts
rows: National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA), enacted in 2005
Three phases: 200 districts in 2006, whole country by 2008
At least 100 days of wage employment a year (150 days for tribals) to at least one adult member of every rural household willing to do unskilled manual work
At least 33% of beneficiaries must be women

blocks.title: MGNREGS numbers
blocks.phrase: A century of days and a third for women: 100 days, 33% women, 150 for tribals; renamed on Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October.
letters: Guaranteed days of work a year

blocks.title: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
rows: Rs 6,000 a year to eligible farmer families in three equal 4-monthly instalments of Rs 2,000
Rs 68,000 crore (Budget Estimate for 2021-22 was Rs 65,000 crore; Revised Estimate Rs 67,500 crore)
The PM-Kisan mobile app with face authentication for e-KYC was launched by the Union Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Yojana (Maharashtra) tops up the Rs 6,000 to Rs 12,000 a year

blocks.title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PM Crop Insurance Scheme)
rows: Premium for commercial and horticultural crops
The individual farmer, not the whole village
Lowest-ever premium, post-harvest cover, mandatory use of technology for quick claim settlement, compensation if sowing is prevented by natural calamities
Kharif crop cycle beginning in June

blocks.title: PM Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
blocks.text: Introduced as part of the Atmanirbhar Bharat package with an investment of **Rs 20,050 crore**, the highest ever in the fishery sector. Fishermen get insurance cover, financial assistance and Kisan Credit Card facility.

blocks.title: PMFBY premium ladder
blocks.phrase: Two for Kharif, one-and-a-half for Rabi, five for cash crops: 2 - 1.5 - 5.

blocks.text: These are items that appeared in recent bank, RRB and RBI papers. They are one-liners, so memorise the who, what and how much.

blocks.title: One-line facts
rows: Settlement scheme for contractual disputes with government suppliers; launched by the Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure)
To be created by the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare under the Ministry of Personnel by combining pension portals (bank portals, ANUBHAV, CPENGRAMS, CGHS)
Madhya Pradesh scheme giving women Rs 1,000 a month
Maharashtra farmer income-support scheme on the lines of PM-Kisan
UPI limit for Retail Direct and IPOs
Raised to Rs 5 lakh in December 2021
Rs 30 lakh (from Rs 15 lakh) from 1 April 2023
RBI retail pilot launched 1 December 2022; one-to-one with fiat currency, held in a digital wallet on mobile devices
IRDAI mission so that every citizen has life, health and property cover
Minimum Rs 1,000, no maximum limit; lock-in of 30 months
Recommended a Universal Basic Income as an alternative to many subsidy-based welfare schemes

blocks.text: For state-level scheme questions, pair the scheme with the state in one picture: **Ladli Behna = Madhya Pradesh (women, Rs 1,000)**, **Namo Shetkari = Maharashtra (farmers)**. For central schemes, pair the scheme with the ministry or agency that runs it.

blocks.title: State schemes pair-up
blocks.phrase: Ladli Behna lives in the heart of India (Madhya Pradesh); Namo Shetkari ploughs in Maharashtra.
letters: Ladli Behna - Madhya Pradesh, Rs 1,000 a month to women
Namo Shetkari - Maharashtra, Rs 6,000 top-up for farmers

revision: PMJDY was announced on 15 August 2014 as the National Mission on Financial Inclusion; tagline Mera Khata Bhagya Vidhata.
Jan Dhan account: no minimum balance, RuPay card with Rs 2 lakh accident cover, overdraft (Rs 10,000) after six months.
PMJJBY, PMSBY and APY were all launched on 9 May 2015.
PMJJBY: age 18-50, Rs 2 lakh life cover, Rs 330 a year; offered by LIC and other life insurers.
PMSBY: age 18-70, Rs 2 lakh accidental death/full disability, Rs 1 lakh partial, Rs 12 a year; general insurers.
Insurance coverage year is 1 June to 31 May, with auto-debit consent on or before 31 May.
APY: age 18-40, guaranteed pension Rs 1,000-5,000 a month from age 60; Government funds any shortfall.
Mudra (8 April 2015): Shishu up to Rs 50,000, Kishore to Rs 5 lakh, Tarun to Rs 10 lakh; no collateral.
Stand Up India (5 April 2016): Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore for at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower per branch; greenfield units.
PMVVY: age 60 and above, 8% assured return for 10 years, via LIC; maximum pension Rs 10,000 a month.
Gold Monetization, Sovereign Gold Bond and Indian Gold Coin were all launched on 5 November 2015.
Startup India launched 16 January 2016; 19-point action plan with a Rs 10,000 crore corpus fund; team reports to DPIIT.
DBT launched 1 January 2013 and uses the Aadhaar Payment Bridge (APB).
MGNREGS: 100 days (150 for tribals), at least 33% women; renamed on 2 October 2009.
PM-KISAN pays Rs 6,000 a year in three instalments of Rs 2,000; PMFBY premium is 2% kharif, 1.5% rabi, 5% commercial.
